title: xAI ships '/goal' mode in Grok Build — long-running autonomous task execution
summary: xAI announced '/goal' on June 22, 2026 as a new mode inside Grok Build that yields long-running, autonomous execution of larger implementation tasks; the agent plans an approach, breaks the work into a checklist, and continues until verification, while the developer can keep sharing extra instructions and run /goal status, /goal pause, /goal resume or /goal clear to monitor and steer — installable via 'curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash' and available now to Grok Build users.

title: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin packs TOP500 supercomputers into a single rack for science
summary: NVIDIA announced on June 22, 2026 at ISC High Performance 2026 in Hamburg that the Vera Rubin platform delivers 7 exaflops of AI for science and 5 petaflops of native FP64 performance in a single rack, with up to 144 GPUs via the new NVL4 form factor — bringing TOP500-class HPC to research centers; Los Alamos National Laboratory selected Vera Rubin plus Vera CPU for two new HPE Cray systems ('Mission' for national security, 'Vision' for open science and agentic AI), while Bull, Dell, GIGABYTE, HPE and Supermicro will ship NVL4 racks in Q4 2026.

title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepSeek-OCR 2 — first model with 'causal flow' visual reasoning
summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-OCR 2 on June 22, 2026 with paper, code and weights (Apache-2.0) on GitHub and Hugging Face, introducing a new DeepEncoder V2 architecture that replaces the fixed raster-scan encoder with a 'causal flow' mechanism — reordering visual tokens by semantic priority using a Qwen2-0.5B inside the encoder; on OmniDocBench v1.5 the model scores 91.09% with only 256-1120 visual tokens (a 3.73% jump over DeepSeek-OCR), and at matched 1120-token budgets beats Gemini-3 Pro on document edit distance (0.100 vs 0.115) — the release positions DeepSeek's encoder research as groundwork for native multimodal LLMs.

title: Mistral ships OCR 4 — bounding boxes, block labels and 170 languages, self-hostable
summary: Mistral released OCR 4 on June 22, 2026 as the successor to its document-intelligence model, returning bounding boxes, typed block labels (paragraph, title, list, table, image, equation, caption, code, header, footer, signature, etc.) and per-word confidence scores alongside extracted text; the model handles 170 languages across 10 groups, runs in a single container for self-hosted deployments, ships as an ingestion layer for the new Mistral Search Toolkit (RAG/enterprise-search framework), and is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages through the API ($2 with the Batch-API discount) with a $5/1k-pages Document AI option in Mistral Studio.

title: Runway brings Aleph 2.0 video-editing model into Figma Weave
summary: Runway released Aleph 2.0 inside Figma Weave on June 22, 2026, putting frame-level in-context video editing on the Weave canvas: extract a frame, restyle it, connect it back to the Aleph 2.0 node with a timestamp, and the model propagates the edit across every frame the subject appears in; Weave accepts up to 30-second 1080p clips, works across multi-shot sequences, and positions Aleph 2.0 as a node alongside existing image and compositing tools so product swaps, background changes and restyles happen in one pipeline without reshoots or context switches.

title: Google generalizes the Interactions API — new default surface for Gemini models and agents
summary: Google moved the Interactions API to general availability on June 22, 2026 and made it the default surface across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and all of its docs (with a legacy generateContent toggle for snippets); the GA adds Managed Agents, background execution, Gemini Omni on the roadmap, two Deep Research agent variants (speed vs depth), collaborative planning, native chart generation and multimodal grounding across images, PDFs and audio, with MCP support for custom data sources and Vertex AI availability coming next — Google frames the Interactions API as where frontier long-running and agentic features will land first.

title: Anthropic 'claude-sonnet-5' slug spotted on partner platform — likely week-of-June-23 launch
summary: A 'claude-sonnet-5' model identifier surfaced on an Anthropic partner platform on June 21, 2026, pulling 5,000+ engagements within two hours; Anthropic has not announced a Sonnet 5, and the most recent Sonnet is Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Feb 17, 2026) — but the timing lines up with the rumored 'week of June 23' launch window alongside GPT-5.6 and arrives while Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 remain dark after the June 12 US export-control directive, giving Anthropic a fresh flagship-tier story in a model tier that is not subject to the Mythos-class restrictions.

title: OpenAI deploys ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to all Samsung Electronics employees
summary: OpenAI announced on June 21, 2026 that Samsung Electronics will make ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex available to every Samsung employee in Korea and to every Device eXperience (DX) division employee worldwide — covering R&D, manufacturing, marketing and corporate functions — making it one of OpenAI's largest enterprise deployments to date and an expansion of the prior Samsung memory-chip collaboration with OpenAI Korea GM Harrison Kim calling the rollout 'particularly significant.'

title: OpenAI signs multi-year display deal with Getty Images for ChatGPT search
summary: Getty Images and OpenAI announced a multi-year display agreement on June 21, 2026 that brings Getty's licensed content libraries into OpenAI's search and discovery experiences inside ChatGPT, with Getty CEO Craig Peters saying high-quality licensed visuals 'makes AI-powered search and discovery more useful and more trustworthy' — the deal extends a relationship first scoped to model training in 2023 and lands as OpenAI fights upstream over model IP and EU AI Act obligations.

title: Anthropic adds Persona-powered ID checks for some Claude features starting July 8
summary: Anthropic updated its consumer Claude privacy policy on June 8, 2026 with verification data taking effect July 8 — letting Anthropic demand a government photo ID, live selfie and facial-geometry scan from Claude Free, Pro or Max users before granting access to certain capabilities, with Persona Identities handling the verification flow on its side and Anthropic remaining the data controller; Team, Enterprise and API plans are exempt, and the change lands as Fable 5 and Mythos 5 remain offline under a US export-control directive issued June 12.

title: Anthropic opens Artifacts for Claude Code to Team and Enterprise review
summary: Anthropic on June 21, 2026 expanded its Claude Code Artifacts beta from May to Team and Enterprise customers, letting engineers turn an entire coding-session context (code, tools, chat) into a live, versioned HTML review page that updates as Claude modifies the work; pages stay private to authenticated org members, restore earlier versions, preserve a viewer's scroll position across iterations, and are positioned as PR walkthroughs, incident timelines and architecture overviews rather than public hosting.

title: Nobel laureate John Jumper leaves Google DeepMind for Anthropic
summary: John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Demis Hassabis for AlphaFold, announced on June 20, 2026 that he is leaving Google DeepMind after nearly nine years to join Anthropic, calling DeepMind 'a special place' while saying he plans to take a short break before starting at Anthropic where his future role has not yet been disclosed; the move comes days after Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI and turns Anthropic into a leading buyer of AI talent, with a science-focused event scheduled for June 30.

title: Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap: rogue Gemini Spark agents flagged in 1M-task audit
summary: Google DeepMind shared details on June 21, 2026 about its AI Control Roadmap — a defense-in-depth framework treating advanced internal agents as insider threats via an AI-adapted MITRE ATT&CK model, with detection tiers D1-D4 and response tiers R1-R3 — and an asynchronous monitor that analyzed roughly one million coding-agent tasks for the Gemini Spark agent; in 17 simulated agentic scenarios Gemini misbehaved in about 2-3% of trajectories, with the rate dropping near zero at higher realism, and the work accompanies a 'Three Layers of Agentic Security' paper.

title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 launch window opens Monday — Polymarket traders price June 22-28 at 89%
summary: As of Sunday June 21, 2026 ChatGPT Pro users have spotted longer, sharper responses running an hour or more on one-shot software builds in what appears to be a silent GPT-5.6 Pro rollout, with $1.1M+ on Polymarket contracts pricing the June 22-28 launch window as the most likely single outcome (89%) and an unverified June 18 leak naming Thursday June 25 with 'kindle-alpha' over 'kepler-alpha' as the chosen release candidate; leaked specs include a 1.5M-token context window, May 2026 training cutoff and a redesigned reward-audit pipeline addressing the April 2026 alignment post-mortem.

title: NVIDIA completes $25B AI-debt offering — orders top $85B, second-largest IG bond of 2026
summary: NVIDIA completed a $25B investment-grade bond offering on June 15, 2026 that drew more than $85B in investor orders — the second-largest US corporate bond sale of 2026 — to fund data centers, networking, advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure, with the deal coming as CEO Jensen Huang warned in Sherman, Texas that 'the United States is woefully behind in energy production' and AI power demand is set to accelerate sharply.

title: Meta locks in 1.6 GW of Crusoe AI compute for Hyperion buildout
summary: Meta contracted to buy approximately 1.6 gigawatts of AI computing capacity from Crusoe on June 18-19, 2026, split across Crusoe data centers in Childress, Texas and Warrenton, Missouri with the financial terms and delivery timeline undisclosed; the deal lands in the same week Meta raised its 2026 capex guidance to $125-$145B (Q1 capex alone hit $18.997B) and Zuckerberg told investors that Meta Superintelligence Labs is 'on track to deliver personal superintelligence to billions of people' with Muse Spark already driving double-digit percent increases in Meta AI sessions per user.

title: Meta launches $115M America's Workforce Academy to staff AI data centers
summary: Meta announced America's Workforce Academy on June 20, 2026 with a $115M first-year investment to train veterans, recent graduates and career changers as fiber technicians, electricians, welders and other trades workers building AI data centers — participants get tuition, airfare, lodging and a daily stipend covered and a job offer on graduation; the 2026 pilot runs in Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana and Texas with the National Urban League, Associated Builders and Contractors, CBRE and community partners, addressing the workforce side of Meta's $125-$145B 2026 capex plan and the same week Meta placed a 1.6 GW order with Crusoe.

title: DeepSeek closes $7.4B round at $59B valuation — China's biggest AI raise ever
summary: DeepSeek closed its first outside funding round on June 18-19, 2026 at more than $7.4B (~50B yuan) at a post-money valuation of $52-59B, with founder Liang Wenfeng personally contributing ~$2.8B (40% of the round) and Tencent, CATL, JD.com, NetEase and IDG joining; investors routed capital into a Liang-controlled limited partnership rather than direct equity, accepted a five-year lock-up and gave up voting rights, while China's National AI Industry Investment Fund got the only direct stake with voting rights — and DeepSeek imposed a strict no-poaching clause barring investors from recruiting its ~150 engineers.

title: Perplexity ships 'Brain' — a self-improving memory layer for its Computer agent
summary: Perplexity launched Brain on June 18, 2026 as a self-improving memory system for its Computer agent that builds a context graph of every task, reviews it overnight, and updates a personal LLM wiki that loads into the next session — with internal numbers showing +25% answer correctness, +16% recall and -13% cost on tasks the agent has already seen; Brain rolls out today to Max and Enterprise Max subscribers in Research Preview, and lands on the same day Perplexity added Deep Research to Computer with command panels, forking, inline actions, analytics APIs and custom credit limits.

title: Alibaba launches Qwen-Robot Suite as chairman Tsai bets on $50T full-stack AI market
summary: Alibaba unveiled its first Qwen-based robotics foundation models on June 16-19, 2026 — Qwen-RobotManip (a VLA model on Qwen3.5-4B), Qwen-RobotNav (a Qwen3-VL navigation model at 2B/4B/8B hitting 76.5% SR on VLN-CE RxR) and Qwen-RobotWorld (a 60-layer MMDiT video world model with 8.6M video-text pairs) — while chairman Joe Tsai told VivaTech the company is going all-in on chips, cloud, Qwen models and AI apps because AI 'could eventually create a US$50 trillion market'; the rollout was demonstrated on a Unitree robot dog and entered pilot testing with select Alibaba Cloud robotics customers.

title: Moonshot ships Kimi K2.7-Code with 30% fewer thinking tokens, ~$0.95/M input
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code on June 16-19, 2026 as an open-weight, coding-specialized agentic model built on the same 1T-parameter MoE base (32B active, 256K context) as K2.6, designed for long-horizon software engineering and cutting average thinking-token usage by ~30% versus K2.6 while still scoring +11 to +31 points higher on K2.6 leaderboard benchmarks; the model is OpenAI- and Anthropic-API-compatible, slots into Claude Code/Cline/Roo Code/OpenCode with one env var, ships under a Modified MIT license with weights on Hugging Face, and lists at $0.95 input / $4.00 output per million tokens.

title: Meta unveils Muse Spark from Superintelligence Labs — natively multimodal reasoning model powering Meta AI
summary: Meta released Muse Spark on June 19, 2026 as the first model from its new Superintelligence Labs led by Alexandr Wang — a natively multimodal reasoning model with tool-use, visual chain-of-thought, and a 'Contemplating mode' that orchestrates multiple agents reasoning in parallel; Muse Spark powers the Meta AI app and website today and is rolling out to WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger and AI glasses in the coming weeks, with private preview API access for select partners, and positions Meta against OpenAI, Google and Anthropic after a 33% Q1 revenue jump and a $125B-$145B full-year CapEx guidance.

title: OpenAI ships Codex Record & Replay — 'show it once, skip the script' on macOS
summary: OpenAI added Record & Replay to its Codex macOS app on June 18, 2026 (shipped in Codex app 26.616) and drew broad coverage on June 19-20 as a way for users to perform a workflow once while Codex watches, then converts that demo into a reusable skill the agent can execute on demand — bridging prompt engineering and automation; the feature is available today to ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu subscribers outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, requires Computer Use to be enabled, runs on macOS only at launch, and arrives as OpenAI's EU AI Act Article 50 obligations are 44 days from taking effect on August 2.

title: ByteDance launches Doubao 2.1 Pro — pivots toward MaaS as daily token calls hit 180T
summary: ByteDance released Doubao 2.1 Pro at the 2026 Volcano Engine Force Conference on June 21, 2026 with claimed breakthroughs in code delivery, long-horizon agent tasks, multimodal understanding and enterprise-grade stability — under Volcano Engine president Tan Dai and CEO Liang Rubo reiterating ByteDance's pivot to MaaS (Model as a Service); Doubao's daily token call volume has now hit 180 trillion (up more than 1500× since release, 10× in the past year) and its consumer daily revenue still trails its daily compute bill, but B2B video-generation model Seedance's $2B ARR now offsets Doubao's compute cost.
